My favorite part of the game is the following scenario:

4. Continuing to scream until their mic cuts off abruptly 
5. Discovering their body afterwards in a physics defying position

This game is extremely fun to play. Luckily my friends and I were looking for a co-op horror game right at this time and I stumbled upon this game. None of us regret it one bit. It's very promising for an early access game.

Pros -
While the game still has jumpscares, it doesn't rely on them very much at all, and instead relies on the natural tension of large, dark areas and the natural activity (or lack thereof) of the ghost in order to build suspense. This means, for me at least, the feeling of dread doesn't end up wearing off and I can still feel genuine fear when going on a new mission, even if I've been there 20 times before, while also letting those jumpscares still be somewhat scary. A win/win in my book.

The voice recognition is something I wasn't sure would work out to be very enjoyable, but boy was I wrong. It creates a great experience, actively speaking to the entity, trying to provoke it to show you what it can do, risking your life for the mission, but it's gotta be done. It's thrilling and fills you with dread. Having the mission react to the things you say is extremely immersive, one of this games biggest strengths.

Immersion as I said, is huge in this game. I always feel like I could actually be in the level. Especially if you are playing in VR, it's hard to be ripped out of the experience, even if you're fucking around with friends, like I was. Being able to be the one in the truck tracking movement and and activity throughout the location is just as thrilling as wandering the house itself looking for activity. It's been hilarious and immersive the several times my friend got impatient waiting for clues and went into the house to insult the ghost only for it to immediately lock the door and begin hunting him. 10/10

Cons - I don't really feel that it's entirely fair to list these as cons, as the game basically JUST came out as I write this, and I have very little to complain about and feel very positively about this game and it's future, but these are things to keep in mind, and that they may and will likely change in the future.

When playing in VR, you can hold a video camera in your hand and carry it around, and others can have a clear view of what you're pointing it at as you move through the house. I would like to see this also become a feature for desktop play, while you still can equip the camera and view it, the angle is very low and bobs sporadically, making things hard to see. You can buy a headmounted camera that I assume fixes this. I am not a high enough level to buy one yet so I'm not sure.

VR players definitely have an advantage in many scenarios as you can turn on equipment such as the EMF reader and the spirit box, then but them on your belt to use them hands-free. I would like for at least the EMF reader to do something similar, instead of turning off when you put it away. It makes a noise when you get a reading, and I think that could stay, while requiring you to pull it out again to see exactly how strong the reading is, I feel that would be a good compromise.

As for VR QOL, my only 2 concerns right now are 1. placing cameras. Currently you grip them by the left or right side in a set direction, and it's only different for each hand it's held in. It can make it difficult to place a camera facing a set direction. I would like to be able to grip cameras from a front angle, as well as from the top, in order to make placing them much easier. And 2. switching hands, currently you have to drop an item manually and catch it if you're fast, or pick it up off the floor in order to switch hands if you don't have room in your belt. Many other games allow you to grab object out of your other hand and I feel it would be very helpful. 

Mission design - Again, keep in mind that I'm writing this in very early access, so I expect this to change at some point. Currently, the only missions are identification. Go in, find clues, deduce the ghost type, leave. I Don't have a problem with map design, but I would like to see other mission types, such as full on removal, as the game talks about you, the identification team, doing the research for a future removal team, missions like that would be great. Another is finding out how the person died and became a ghost, the journal mentions a few times about death and people becoming a ghost. Finding clues about the death of the ghost would be a very interesting mission design and I'd love to see it come to light.

Sanity is also something I expect to become something much more than it is currently as the game goes on. I feel that is obvious but I will give my 2 cents anyway for complete transparency. Right now, with my current understanding, it doesn't matter until you hit 50% at which point the ghost becomes more aggressive against you. This on it's own is interesting and can be useful for drawing the ghost out, but I would like to see more, such as hallucinations, both visual and auditory. There's not much more I can say on this, anything I could is just as obvious as that so I won't bother, and again, expect changes to this.

Lastly, when you die, you become a ghost and wander the map as an invisible entity. I think this has a lot planned for the future, but currently that's all there is to it. I think it would be extremely interesting if you could interact with the world in a similar way to the spirit your team is still hunting. Things like flicking the lights, writing short phrases on walls, or maybe being able to speak in a ghostly filter for just a couple seconds to give them a clue, would be very fun and make it so you're not just a passive and clueless observer if you are killed. If done in a way where it isn't always clear if the interaction is between the hostile spirit or your fallen friend, it would be possibly the most unique thing I've ever seen in a co-op horror game.

All in all, this game is a steal at it's current $15 price, and I got it on sale for less than $13! Even if you want to wait to play it when it's more developed, pick it up now! I have no issues recommending this to anyone, and I anticipate a very bright future in those dark corridors.

Phasmophobia is the perfect game if you’ve ever wanted to scream like a toddler. I played Phasmophobia for around 3 hours straight after buying it and had one hell of a time doing so with my friends... This is without a doubt a game you want to play with someone you know, preferably 3/4 people. I have said it before and I will say it again: Indie developers are the saviours of the gaming industry - where the endlessly funded triple A studios fail, your every day gamer with a knack for game development pulls through with something amazing, as proven by Kinetic Games and studios such as Iron Gate AB (the ones that made Valheim). 

The game itself is nothing complex but extremely fun and scary even without VR - I would probably buy a VR headset just for this game alone - and it runs perfectly on my PC without any real performance issues, bugs or glitches, so far at least. 

I can not praise the game enough for being innovative in a time where most games are copy and paste. And the best thing about Phasmophobia in my opinion is the accessible price: 10 bucks for a game with this much potential and content already!? Bargain. My only wish is that they add achievements to the game, I think that would be cool because it would incentivise us to do XYZ and grind for some of them. Other than that, I highly recommend this game.

This game is fun, but absolutely requires friends to be fun (in my opinion). The core gameplay is actually quite slow, and that was a problem for me at first before I could get into it with friends. It was a little scary at first but that kind of turns into comedy in a group setting. I never felt truly terrified while playing this game, but I did get a couple great spooks out of it. 

What I would love for this game is to go "off the rails" for horror. By that, I mean there needs to be waaay more unscripted horror events. The scares in this game come in a formula. Current formula: Explore house, find "the room", drop gear, wait for hunt, get "scare". MAYBE get a ghostly popup or two in the meantime. This game needs more little terrors that are outside the standard loop. Good examples would be: you turn around to leave a room and the ghost is at the door watching you, but it disappears when you see it. Maybe you see a shape in a window as you approach the house, or more spooky sounds while you're doing stuff. Most of all, this game needs more scary sounds. I don't mean it needs to rely on jumpscares, but if the ghosts were doing more spooky whispers and noises, I'd be way more on edge.

As far as a fun little ghost explore game to play with friends, this game absolutely nails its goal. It's fun and certainly has scary moments, especially when new to the game. The times I was scared was when I didn't know the map layout yet and didn't know where to go during hunts. As far as being a truly terrifying ghost game, it falls short for me.

Phasmophobia is a fantastic co-op horror game, especially in the beginning. Those first 20-30 hours are filled with tension, excitement, and genuine scares. The atmosphere, eerie locations, and unpredictable ghost encounters keep you constantly on edge.

However, after around 100 hours, the fear factor starts to fade. Ghost hunts become more routine, and you’ll find yourself going through the usual motions—gathering evidence, identifying the ghost type, and moving on. While it’s still enjoyable with friends, the initial thrill wears off as you become more familiar with the maps and gameplay.

For me and my group, Phasmophobia is great when you have an hour to spare between other games. It’s fun to unlock new equipment, but beyond that, the game gradually loses its horror appeal. That said, playing solo can still provide a solid and tense experience.

Considering I have over 150+ hours played at the time of this review, I would say it was money well spent in terms of value.

Phasmophobia quickly went viral, but beyond the hype generated by streaming and YouTube videos, is all this hype justified?

The game’s most original feature is its voice recognition. The ghost you’re hunting can hear you, even if you don’t activate the in-game push-to-talk function. It can reply to you (via a spirit box), react to what you say, and so on.

But what makes the game even better is the range of tools at your disposal and the strategy you need to put in place. You won’t simply go from place to place hunting a ghost; you’ll have to prepare – and therefore buy equipment – before you can begin an investigation. Because that’s what Phasmophobia is all about – it’s an investigation game: having the right tools, finding the room where the ghost is, using the tools to determine what type of ghost it is, gathering evidence, and making your escape (alive or dead).

And all of this is even more fun with friends; everyone will have a role to play – the scaredy-cat will stay in the van, the more adventurous will be chased by the ghost – and even though the locations are fairly limited (fewer than 10), each experience will be quite different.

Where it falls short (for me, at least – it’s rather subjective) is the single-player mode. Technically, it’s the same thing as it’s a private game, but the locations designed for 3–4 people feel far too big, whilst the smaller ones are rather boring. Honestly, I think this is a game best suited to co-op play with friends (or strangers).

The game has a few bugs and crashes occasionally; the content is rather limited in terms of locations, but it’s an Early Access title that looks quite promising overall.

I am writing this review as somebody who is not a fan of horror games. Usually due to one of two reasons (or both); they rely on cheap jump scares instead of building worthwhile suspension, or they are simply a slog to play through. 

With that in mind, I didn’t think I would like Phasmophobia. Alas, my expectations for this game were completely subverted. Not only is this one of the best horror games I’ve ever played in a long time, it’s also one of the best games to come out this year. Let me explain why.

[h1]Ghost hunting’s no easy job...[/h1]

Phasmophobia’s gameplay loop is something that appears simplistic on the surface level, but becomes so much more as you go deeper into it. You play as a ghost hunter, and your overall task is to travel to abandoned locations and identify what type of ghost inhabits them. 

This task is achieved by doing smaller tasks that provide clues as to what type of ghost you’re dealing with. Whilst doing this, the ghost will tend to mess around with the player, whether it be by moving objects, creating audio hallucinations, turning on sinks, etc. Overtime the ghost will become more dangerous and will sometimes hunt the player. 

Due to the number of ways you can identify a ghost, and the unpredictability of the AI, the gameplay doesn’t really get too repetitive. While not perfect, the AI provides an intense and sometimes terrifying experience that’ll keep you on edge until you’ve completed your task. Even after playing for a number of hours, the game doesn’t lose its grip, and that is thanks to both the design of the AI and the wide range of methods used to identify the ghost.

However, the game can struggle when it comes to pacing. I’ve had the occasional match where identifying the ghost was near impossible due to the ghost’s apparent lack of interest in doing anything. When this sort of thing happens, it can become a drag, especially on larger maps. Also doesn’t help that your character moves like a snail…

[h1]They can hear you…[/h1]

A brilliant way of summarising Phasmophobia is that it’s basically one of those cheesy ghost hunting TV shows, but in video game form. One of Phasmophobia’s most unique features relates perfectly to this idea. The player has the ability to communicate with the ghost.

It is essential that you come into Phasmophobia with a microphone. Some ghosts require you to use one. While not all ghosts will be willing to speak with you, a good way of knowing more about the ghost is to simply talk to it. It’s a feature that is completely unique and has the potential to produce horrifying results. The only thing that lets this feature down is the same text to speech voice being used for all of the ghosts. 

It’s features like this that give Phasmophobia such an intense atmosphere. Not only can the ghost interact with you and the environment around you, but you can also interact with the ghost. Calling the ghost by its name could irritate it, and if you ask it to turn off the lights, it might just do that. There could be absolutely nothing happening at all, and yet the game will still keep you on edge.

[h1]My Final Thoughts[/h1]

If it isn’t apparent enough at this point, I definitely recommend Phasmophobia, especially if you are a fan of horror games. This is one you shouldn’t miss. If you are looking for a game to play with a group of friends, this should keep you entertained for plenty of hours. If you are willing to put up with slow pacing, then this is a game that I cannot recommend enough.

Phasmophobia was released in September 2020, exclusively for PC, and remains in early access on Steam as of now. It offers such a captivating experience, where you and three friends step into the roles of paranormal investigators. With each mission, you have access to a variety of equipment, which unlocks as you progress, making each investigation feel even more rewarding. Your goal is to explore haunted locations, collect valuable information, and share your findings with other ghost hunters. It’s wonderfully nostalgic, evoking the thrill of games like Slenderman and Pacify, providing hours of fun with your friends.

You have two ways to engage in the game—either assist your team remotely from the safety of a monitoring computer or step right into the eerie atmosphere to gather evidence firsthand. But be warned, venturing into the haunted locations comes with its own risks.

The game gives you access to a wide array of ghost-hunting tools, including spirit boxes, ultraviolet lights, crucifixes, night vision cameras, EMF detectors, and flashlights, so you’re always prepared for what lies ahead. Your mission is to identify the ghost or demon responsible for the haunting, and once you do, you return to your van and escape the location, completing the investigation. With ten different types of ghosts to discover, each encounter feels unique and exciting.

One of the most delightful aspects of Phasmophobia is its speech recognition system. Spirits can hear you when you speak, and they can even respond to specific words. Certain tools require you to say particular phrases, and some demons get agitated when their name is called out, which adds such a thrilling and immersive layer to the experience.

If you’re someone who loves a fully immersive experience, Phasmophobia is also compatible with virtual reality, which makes it even more perfect for those who want to feel like they’re truly there. At just $13.99, it’s such a fantastic pick for October, especially with Halloween around the corner.

When I saw a new co-op horror game pop up in my suggested titles I was intrigued but was a bit cautious since I assumed it wouldn't do a great job of building a scary environment and rely mainly on quick jump scares. This game does a great job of creating an environment that offsets you and relies on more atmospheric horror. While it can be seen as jump scary for you to turn around and see the ghost in the same room with you it is never really right up in your face and having the secondary goal of giving you a heart attack. The concept is great and is best played with friends. You grab a bunch of equipment and head out to a recently haunted location with some information and investigate what kind of ghost you are dealing with. Different ghosts have different weaknesses and abilities. The ghost hunting equipment is fun and the game is well thought out that each team member plays a particular role since you can only hold up to three equipment pieces at once. As mentioned the environment is pretty scary and the sound design is well done. Popping into a room and asking if there is anyone there only to hear the word "here" behind you or "die" through a spirit box can send some chills down your spine. There's a mix of locations and as you continue to play you can get some more advanced equipment to help you in your investigations. 

[h1]The Minor Gripes[/h1]
There are a few things that are still a bit rough around the edges from model clipping to things that need graphical improvements. The game devs have done a pretty good job of rolling out a lot of patches to fix some of these issues so that is a big plus. My hope is that as these patches continue to optimize the game more content is also created. The game isn't that strong as a solo game so I wouldn't jump into this if you intend to only play by yourself. At the same time the multiplayer in some cases; especially in the larger maps should be expanded to a bigger party size. At the moment you can only play with 4 people to a party and some of the bigger maps such as the school and the asylum still feel like you are undermanned. [h1][b]Phasmophobia[/b][/h1]
[i]Phasmophobia[/i] is a coop horror game in which up to 4 players have to figure out what kind of ghost is haunting the place they have been sent to.

[b]Gameplay[/b]

Your goal in this game is to find out what type of ghost is spooking around in a certain location. You need to gather evidence with multiple tools to figure out what kind of ghost it is – be careful you might get hunted if you anger the ghost too much, which could result in an early death. 

[b]Personal Note[/b]

There are a lot of ways to get the ghost to hunt you. So far, the most effective method is to insult the ghost but singing random songs or sea shanties seem to be very effective as well. 

Yelling “[i]Hunt me daddy! Uwu[/i]” not only made me lose the last ounce of respect my friends had for me but also resulted in a hunt – kinda worth it I guess. 

I also tried to flirt with the ghost which wasn’t effective at all – maybe saying “[i]I see you throwing stuff around in the room, I'd rather throw you on the bed[/i]” just wasn’t the right approach for the ghost I’ve encountered.

[b]Rating[/b]
[list][b]Pros[/b]
[*] The different ghosts are unique while sharing some common behavior
[*] The game is actually spooky and intense
[*] Multiple maps and RNG keeps the game interesting
[*] It’s a 4 player coop but you also can play it with less than 4 people
[*] The game runs in standard and VR mode
[*] [Strike]Beta version features upcoming and experimental features and content[/Strike] (1)
[/list]
[list][b]Cons[/b]
[*] Progression system is very basic as of now (2)
[*] Without much knowledge it can be hard to get better at this game
[*] Early Access (3)
[/list]
(1) [Strike]As of now (21.01.2021) there are some new experimental features regarding the ghost AI and temperature changes which make the game more interesting. There were also daily updates for those things including fixes.[/Strike]

(2) The progression system is super basic – which isn’t an issue for me personally, especially since the game is in Early Access – for some people this could be a bigger issue though.

(3) Phasmophobia is an Early Access title which might be a big problem for some people. There is only 1 person working on this game so the progress regarding new content could be a bit slower than usual. There could be more bugs than usual as well. ([i]I’ve read multiple times that the dev hired two more people to help, but I’m not sure if that is true[/i])

[b]Conclusion[/b]

It’s a great game and it is a lot of fun when you play with some friends. It has the right amount of spooky elements that made me jump and scream like a little baby. It’s worth to check out the Beta as well, since most experimental features and content will be accessible there first.

[b]7.5 / 10[/b]

[b]Basic Breakdown[/b]: Phasmophobia, developed and published by [b]Kinetic Games[/b], is a 4 player co-op game where you take the role of ghost hunters. Except you don't get to kill/take the ghost away, you are only given tools in order to identify each ghost and get pay out by the end of it (If you survive, OooOooOooO), that then lets you buy more equipment to find and identify the ghosts easier as you progress and get more knowledgeable with the game.

[b]Graphics[/b]: Honestly really good, it's not ground breaking graphics, but they're perfect for the type of game it is and really sets the scene enough for that tension to start building up even easier. Textures are honestly really nice in the maps that are currently available and I can't wait to see what more they add to this gem!

[b]Soundtrack[/b]: There isn't one, but ambient, unsettling hums when you get into the building and more ambient noises when you get outside/to the van, but somehow it's such a relief if you've been stuck inside the building hearing nothing but unsettling ambiance and ghost footsteps as you hide for your life. The sound effects of each item also sounds really clean and well made. 

Now, to move along to the ghost noises, Ohmygod. Can we take a moment to appreciate how good these are?! They're horrifying and I hate them, they unsettle the absolute crap out of me, but they're so good!

[b]Menu[/b]: Simple design, good set of options, allows you to copy the room key to clipboard (this is a new feature, but I can't not mention this), makes my life so much easier and I love it!

This game also does what I honestly wish more games would do, and it gives you an idle room whilst you might be waiting for a buddy to join up, you can play basketball, throw paint cans around, it sounds silly and like it isn't a whole lot, but having a room to just chill in whilst you're inviting a party, or you're just wanting a break from the constant jumpscares, this is great. Other games, take note; do this!

[b]Final Conclusion[/b]: Honestly, as someone that is not into horror, I'm so very glad I took the dive into this game and played it just before it went absolutely viral so I got a completely raw and unbiased opinion on this game; hands down, this is one of the best cooperative horror games I've ever played and probably will for a very long time. So much in this game is so well thought out, and you can clearly see the work they're putting into it.

I've not touched much on the fact this game is also playable in VR (I'm assuming this is why movement speed needed to be very slow, other than the fact it also scares the crap out of me to very slowly shamble away from imminent death, whilst I scream my head off).

The atmosphere in this game is horrendously good, after 88 hours, I still get terrified when ghost boi's decide to come breathe in my ear to let me know  of their presence. The movement adds to the tension. The game play is simple and yet simultaneously full of depth. 

Another unique thing about this game is the fact it's always listening. You swear or say certain key things to upset your resident ghost friend, it'll come for you, throw stuff around etc. Sometimes there is nothing more fun than to stand in the doorway calling it obscene names until it finally does something or you step in the house only for it to instantly hunt and murder you. Being quiet during hunts also increases tension, and just general atmosphere within the games.

I'm so very excited to see where this game goes and where the improvements take it. Despite the fact that is has bugs (Yes, this amazing game is an early access game, it will have bugs, chill out), they're never too game breaking and they're constantly working to fix them. [b]Kinetic[/b] honestly deserve all the support over this incredible game. I can honestly thank it for getting me into horror games just that little bit more.

I 100000000% recommend this game. It's not just a cheap jumpscare.
